description: Our team brings together artists, graphic designers, and 3D designers who are passionate about space, digital art, and visual storytelling. We are fascinated by the history of NASA space missions, particularly the abandoned equipment left on the Moon and Mars, such as rovers, lunar vehicles, landing modules, and scientific instruments. We aim to combine art, design, and 3D modeling to recreate these objects and tell their stories.
summary:
Silent Explorers is an interactive educational website that turns NASA's space hardware into stories people can explore. We built an experience where each explorer (currently the Mars missions Opportunity, Ingenuity and InSight) comes with an interactive 3D model, a first-person story inspired by its real mission, its scientific discoveries, and its final destination.

The problem: mission achievements are scattered across technical reports, archives and mission pages, which makes them hard for a wider audience to find and understand. Once a mission ends, the story of its spacecraft fades from view.

We bring verified NASA data (mission archives, images and 3D resources) together into one visual narrative, created with Blender and Three.js. This makes science accessible to students and curious people everywhere, preserves the legacy of space exploration, and inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
Detailed Project Description

Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars

Our project is a concept for a future interactive educational website dedicated to the equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after NASA space missions. The main idea is to tell the stories behind these objects and show that even abandoned equipment is an important part of the history of space exploration.

How Will the Project Work?

We plan to create a website where users will be able to explore abandoned space equipment through photographs, 3D models, and interesting informational materials. Each object will have its own story, including its purpose and information about the space mission in which it was used. We want to focus especially on the visual design and user-friendly experience of the website.

Project Benefits

Our idea combines education, science, and modern digital technologies. It will make information about space exploration more accessible, interesting, and easier to understand. Instead of simply reading facts, users will be able to discover the history of space exploration through visual materials and an interactive format.

Expected Impact

We hope that the future website will encourage people to become more interested in astronomy, space technology, and the history of exploring other planets. It will also help raise awareness of the importance of preserving space heritage.

Tools and Resources

During the concept development stage, we used Blender to work with 3D visualizations. We also used figures and 3D models from NASA's official website as visual references for the future project. These resources will help us create a more realistic and engaging website. The main digital product we plan to develop is a website.

Creativity and Factors Considered by the Team

The uniqueness of our idea lies in its unusual perspective on space exploration. Instead of focusing only on successful missions, we want to explore the objects left behind on other celestial bodies and reveal the stories behind them. During the planning process, our team considered the accuracy of information, the historical value of the objects, the quality of future 3D visualizations, creative design, and website usability.

Our goal is to create more than just an informational website. We want to build an engaging digital space where every object left on the Moon or Mars can tell its own story.
